name: pseudouridine_effect_check_v1
purpose: Test whether a pseudouridine modification's effect is constant across constructs, which is the unverified assumption that licenses every ranking claim this project makes about a modified panel.
authorized_by: user, 2026-10-20: 'do the m1Ψ check first and then start the MPRA acquisition'

why_this_matters.the_assumption: Every uridine in the molecules the collaborator will assay is N1-methylpseudouridine. No component in the stack represents it: ViennaRNA, strand_rnafold_calibration_v1 and RiboNN all treat the sequence as canonical U. The project has therefore argued that because the modification is CONSTANT ACROSS THE PANEL, it does not confound a RANKING of constructs.
why_this_matters.what_that_argument_needs: That argument requires the modification's effect to be sequence-independent, so that it shifts every construct by the same factor and leaves the order unchanged.
why_this_matters.status_before_this_check: Recorded as unverified in configs/transcript_inputs_v1_2026-10-19.json and in reports/remaining_limitations_before_candidate_design_2026-10-19.md section A1. There was no evidence either way.
why_this_matters.consequence_if_the_effect_is_construct_d: The ranking argument does not hold. Predictions made on the unmodified sequence would not order the modified molecules, and every ranking claim in this project inherits that limitation.

disclosure_about_declaration_order.statement: These criteria were written before any statistical test was computed, but AFTER the raw per-construct values were visible during inspection of the workbook.
disclosure_about_declaration_order.why_it_is_recorded: The in-solution half-life validation (external_validation_leppek_v1) was declared before its numbers were seen at all. This check is a weaker guarantee and should not be read as the same standard.
disclosure_about_declaration_order.mitigation: The decision rule below is a fixed threshold on a ratio of dispersions, not a p-value chosen after the fact, and both readouts are reported whatever they show.

modification_identity.what_the_paper_used: pseudouridine, recorded as PSU against Unmodified in the source sheets
modification_identity.consequence: This check tests Ψ, not m1Ψ. A construct-dependent Ψ effect is evidence that a uridine modification's effect CAN depend on sequence; it is not a measurement of m1Ψ. A constant Ψ effect would likewise not prove m1Ψ is constant. This limitation cannot be removed with this dataset.

source.paper: Leppek K, Byeon GW, Kladwang W, et al. Nat Commun 13, 1536 (2022).

sheets.Fig_S8b: in-solution half-life in hours, 6 constructs x {Unmodified, PSU}, with reported errors
sheets.Fig_4a: Nluc and Fluc luminescence, 6 paired constructs as a 3 x 2 factorial of three 5'UTRs by two CDSs, 4 replicates per cell, at 6 h and 24 h

source.redistribution: Not republished. The hash is pinned so the source can be re-acquired; only derived metrics are published.

in_solution_half_life.statistic: per-construct log2 fold change, PSU over Unmodified
in_solution_half_life.uncertainty: propagated from the reported half-life errors on both arms

protein_output.statistic: per-construct difference in mean log2(Nluc/Fluc), PSU minus Unmodified, computed separately at 6 h and 24 h
protein_output.why_normalised: Nluc is the construct's reporter and Fluc the co-transfected control; the ratio removes transfection efficiency, and the magnitudes in the sheet are consistent with that role
protein_output.uncertainty: within-cell standard deviation over the 4 replicates

declared_criteria.question: Is the modification's effect constant across constructs?
declared_criteria.primary_statistic: the ratio of the between-construct standard deviation of the effect to the median within-construct uncertainty of the effect
declared_criteria.why_a_dispersion_ratio: With six constructs, a significance test has almost no power and a null result would be uninformative. Comparing the spread of the effect against the noise on the effect answers the question that matters: is the variation in the effect larger than the measurement can explain.
secondary: the factorial breakdown: does the effect differ by 5'UTR and by CDS
the range of fold changes, reported directly, because a reader can judge a 1.2-fold against a 2.7-fold effect without any statistic
whether the two readouts agree with each other, since they are independent measurements
declared_criteria.both_outcomes_are_reportable: A constant effect would support the project's ranking argument for Ψ and would be reported as such, with the m1Ψ caveat intact. A construct-dependent effect undermines it and will be reported in the same place.

what_this_cannot_establish: Anything quantitative about m1Ψ, which is a different nucleoside from the Ψ used here.
Anything about the project's own construct, which is not in this dataset.
That a constant effect would make the predictions correct; it would only mean the modification does not reorder them.
A significance claim. Six constructs cannot support one, and none is made.
